top_categories.workout_context: 334 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
At Tour of Wessex, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
52ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
17,388ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
334 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 334 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Tour of Wessex. Train it until it feels boring.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 17,388ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Tour of Wessex's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before race day.
Low-cadence force work supports 17,388ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

Road-specific control matters at Tour of Wessex. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 334 miles.
17,388ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.

race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 334 miles: 80–100g carbs/hour from mile 1 — don’t wait until you’re hungry. Practice your exact race-day nutrition in every long training ride. Carry backup calories. 334 miles burns 8,000–12,000+ calories — you cannot replace them all, but you must try.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Over Under, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 334 miles of mixed terrain in Langport, Somerset, England (classic three-day format, ran through at least 2023; Yeovil was on-route, not the event base).
